what_happened: backfill-file-scope.sh already existed and reuses the harvester, but cannot fix #410 as-is since its plan uses a Territory Contract table instead of per-phase Files-to-modify blocks; a repo-wide sweep found only 1 of 16 active plans missing the field (vs 130 of ~971 archived), which sharpens the severity-tier decision for the plan phase

Ran the per-phase Files-to-modify gap sweep at plan time (16 active plans, 116 phase blocks): 13 omitting phases across 3 plans, exactly 1 whole-plan miss. That measurement converted the dispatch's open SCOPE-2 'decide the tier' item into a decided two-tier design (per-phase warn, whole-plan error) with no guesswork.

test-validate-artifact.sh resolves the script under test as $REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh BEFORE its source-store sibling. Run from the source store, git rev-parse --show-toplevel yields the nvim config repo, so the suite silently exercises THAT repo's deployed validator instead of the edit under test. Recorded as a Risk row and a Phase 3 task constraint (verify by direct source-store invocation; run the suite only from the deployed BimodalLogic tree after redeploy).

Deployed .claude/ core tree is stale: .claude-extensions.json records source_git_head f86b736 while agent-system HEAD is db6aeae. Research reported them matching at research time, so the gap opened since. Plan absorbs it as Phase 1 (redeploy + record gate baseline) so a later gate failure is classifiable as NEW vs EXPECTED.

Phase 3's test fixture (b) initially asserted the harvester returns [] for a sentinel-only phase, but the two-phase fixture's Phase 2 anchor path makes the whole-plan harvest non-empty (the harvester unions across the whole plan, not per-phase). Caught by manual direct-invocation verification before committing; corrected to assert the harvest equals exactly the one-element anchor array.
